name: Rosa Vance
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember learning where the harbor looks most level from a bench.” On Saturday, near Ferris Deli, Rosa asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I have always been seasick. I told the skipper which bench has the best steady horizon for talking after a trip.
appearance: Rosa has a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape, a small notch in the left eyebrow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a black overshirt with pearl buttons. It usually goes with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. When somebody else has the floor, Rosa steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Rosa has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Rosa knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To provide a steady place to meet on land.
family: Elizabeth Campos is Rosa’s cousin raised in the same household. Rosa gets to change the plan. Elizabeth offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The expensive summer*, Elizabeth says, “I make fancy cakes. I delivered one small enough to share without pretending it was a feast.”
connections: Cyrus Berg. A steady patch of horizon by the café makes a place for the first shore payday lunch.

reactions.situation: An owner offers the former skipper a title with no clear duties
reactions.response: Rosa asks what actual work, hours and wage go with the shore title.

reactions.response: Rosa asks them to describe one concrete thing that will be different tomorrow.
